info.name: Kalshi Trade API Manual Endpoints account market API

params.name: series_ticker
params.description: Series ticker - the series that contains the target market

params.name: ticker
params.description: Market ticker - unique identifier for the specific market

params.name: start_ts
params.description: Start timestamp (Unix timestamp). Candlesticks will include those ending on or after this time.

params.name: end_ts
params.description: End timestamp (Unix timestamp). Candlesticks will include those ending on or before this time.

params.name: period_interval
params.description: Time period length of each candlestick in minutes. Valid values are 1 (1 minute), 60 (1 hour), or 1440 (1 day).

params.name: include_latest_before_start
params.description:
If true, prepends the latest candlestick available before the start_ts. This synthetic candlestick is created by:
1. Finding the most recent real candlestick before start_ts
2. Projecting it forward to the first period boundary (calculated as the next period interval after start_ts)
3. Setting all OHLC prices to null, and `previous_price` to the close price from the real candlestick

items.docs:
Time period length of each candlestick in minutes. Valid values: 1 (1 minute), 60 (1 hour), 1440 (1 day).
Candlesticks for markets that settled before the historical cutoff are only available via `GET /historical/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks`. See [Historical Data](https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/historical_data) for details.

items.docs: Endpoint for getting all trades for all markets. A trade represents a completed transaction between two users on a specific market. Each trade includes the market ticker, price, quantity, and timestamp information. This endpoint returns a paginated response. Use the 'limit' parameter to control page size (1-1000, defaults to 100). The response includes a 'cursor' field - pass this value in the 'cursor' parameter of your next request to get the next page. items.docs: Endpoint for getting the current order book for a specific market.  The order book shows all active bid orders for both yes and no sides of a binary market. items.docs: Endpoint for getting data about a specific series by its ticker.  A series represents a template for recurring events that follow the same format and rules (e.g., "Monthly Jobs Report", "Weekly Initial Jobless Claims", "Daily Weather in NYC"). Series define the structure, settlement sources, and metadata that will be applied to each recurring event instance within that series.

params.name: include_volume
params.description: If true, includes the total volume traded across all events in each series.

params.name: min_updated_ts
params.description: Filter series with metadata updated after this Unix timestamp (in seconds). Use this to efficiently poll for changes.

items.docs: Endpoint for getting data about multiple series with specified filters.  A series represents a template for recurring events that follow the same format and rules (e.g., "Monthly Jobs Report", "Weekly Initial Jobless Claims", "Daily Weather in NYC"). This endpoint allows you to browse and discover available series templates by category.

items.docs:
Filter by market status. Possible values: `unopened`, `open`, `closed`, `settled`. Leave empty to return markets with any status.
 - Only one `status` filter may be supplied at a time.
 - Timestamp filters will be mutually exclusive from other timestamp filters and certain status filters.

 | Compatible Timestamp Filters | Additional Status Filters| Extra Notes |
 |------------------------------|--------------------------|-------------|
 | min_created_ts, max_created_ts | `unopened`, `open`, *em

items.docs:
Endpoint for retrieving candlestick data for multiple markets.

- Accepts up to 100 market tickers per request
- Returns up to 10,000 candlesticks total across all markets
- Returns candlesticks grouped by market_id
- Optionally includes a synthetic initial candlestick for price continuity (see `include_latest_before_start` parameter)
